blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 4 + 5 \cdot 8 + 7 \cdot 16 + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh A.G.P. series hai: har term (A.P. ka number) \(\times\) (G.P. ka number) hai. Is ka sum nikalne ke liye koi ratta formula nahi, hum book wala tareeqa lagayenge: \(r\) se multiply karo, ek jagah shift karo, aur minus karo.
Pehle factors \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) A.P. hain aur doosre factors \(2, 4, 8, 16, \ldots\) G.P. hain jis ka ratio 2 hai.
Plan: \(T_n\) likho, \(S_n\) ke neeche \(2S_n\) ek jagah shift kar ke likho, minus karo, beech wali G.P. ka sum lagao, aur \(S_n\) nikal lo.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 4 + 5 \cdot 8 + \cdots\); A.P. \(a = 1, d = 2\); G.P. \(b = 2, r = 2\)
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\), yani \(n\) terms ka sum.
Tareeqa: Wahi tareeqa jo 6.8.1 mein seekha: pehle \(S_n\) likho, phir poori series ko G.P. ke ratio \(r\) se multiply kar ke \(rS_n\) ek jagah right shift kar ke neeche likho, phir minus karo. Beech mein ek seedhi G.P. ban jati hai jis ka sum hum formula se nikal lete hain. A.G.P. ke sum ka koi ratta formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh tareeqa yaad rakhein.

\(n\)th term
\[a_n = 1 + (n - 1)2 = 2n - 1\]
\[b_n = 2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n}\]
\[T_n = (2n - 1)2^{n}\]
Kyun: A.P. ka \(n\)th term \(2n - 1\) (odd numbers) aur G.P. ka \(n\)th term \(2^n\) hai, kyunke \(2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{1 + n - 1} = 2^n\). Aakhri term likhne ke liye \(T_n\) zaroori hai, isi liye pehle yeh nikala.

\(S_n\) aur \(2S_n\) likhein
\[S_n = 1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 2^{2} + 5 \cdot 2^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + (2n - 1)2^{n}\]
\[2S_n = 1 \cdot 2^{2} + 3 \cdot 2^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (2n - 3)2^{n} + (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
Kyun: Har term ko 2 se multiply karne se 2 ki power ek barh jati hai: \(1 \cdot 2\) ban gaya \(1 \cdot 2^2\). Ise ek jagah right shift kar ke likhte hain taake same power wale terms ek doosre ke neeche aayein. \(S_n\) ka second-last term \((2n - 3)2^{n-1}\) tha, jo \(2\) se multiply ho kar \((2n - 3)2^n\) bana.

\(S_n\) mein se \(2S_n\) minus karein
\[-S_n = 1 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 2^{2} + 2 \cdot 2^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + 2 \cdot 2^{n} - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
\[-S_n = 2 + 2(2^{2} + 2^{3} + \cdots + 2^{n})\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
Kyun: Left side: \(S_n - 2S_n = -S_n\). Right side par same power wale terms ka farq hamesha A.P. ka \(d = 2\) aata hai: \((3 - 1)2^2\), \((5 - 3)2^3\), waghera. Pehla term \(1 \cdot 2\) akela reh jata hai aur \(2S_n\) ka aakhri term \((2n - 1)2^{n+1}\) minus ho jata hai.
Dhyan dein: yeh aakhri minus term bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai.

Bracket wali G.P. ka sum
\[2^{2} + 2^{3} + \cdots + 2^{n}\]
\[= \dfrac{4(2^{n-1} - 1)}{2 - 1}\]
\[= 2^{n+1} - 4\]
Kyun: Bracket mein G.P. hai: pehla term \(4\), ratio \(2\). Powers 2 se \(n\) tak hain, is liye terms ki tadaad \(n - 1\) hai, \(n\) nahi. Formula \(\frac{a_1(r^m - 1)}{r - 1}\) lagaya (\(r > 1\) ho to yeh shakal aasaan rehti hai). \(4 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n+1}\).

Simplify kar ke \(S_n\) nikalein
\[-S_n = 2 + 2(2^{n+1} - 4)\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
\[= 2 + 2^{n+2} - 8\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
\[= -6 + 2^{n+1}[2 - (2n - 1)]\]
\[= -6 + (3 - 2n)2^{n+1}\]
\[S_n = 6 + (2n - 3)2^{n+1}\]
\[= 6 + (4n - 6)2^{n}\]
Kyun: G.P. ka sum rakha, bracket khola. \(2 \cdot 2^{n+1} = 2^{n+2}\), aur isay \(2 \cdot 2^{n+1}\) likh kar \(2^{n+1}\) common liya. \(2 - 8 = -6\). Phir dono taraf \(-1\) se multiply kiya taake \(S_n\) positive ho. Aakhir mein \((2n - 3) \cdot 2 = 4n - 6\), jo answer key wali shakal hai.

Tasdeeq
\[n = 1:\ 6 + (-2)(2) = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ 6 + (2)(4) = 14 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har sum formula ki sab se aasaan tasdeeq: \(n = 1\) rakho to jawab pehla term aana chahiye, aur \(n = 2\) rakho to pehle do terms ka jama. Agar dono match ho jayein to formula sahi hai. Yahan \(S_1 = 2\) aur \(S_2 = 2 + 12 = 14\), dono match.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^{2} + 6 \cdot 3^{3} + 8 \cdot 3^{4} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh A.G.P. series hai: har term (A.P. ka number) \(\times\) (G.P. ka number) hai. Is ka sum nikalne ke liye koi ratta formula nahi, hum book wala tareeqa lagayenge: \(r\) se multiply karo, ek jagah shift karo, aur minus karo.
Yahan aage wale numbers \(2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots\) A.P. hain aur 3 ki powers G.P. hain, ratio 3.
Plan: \(T_n\) likho, \(3S_n\) shift kar ke neeche likho, minus karo, G.P. ka sum lagao, aur \(S_n\) nikalo.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^2 + 6 \cdot 3^3 + \cdots\); A.P. \(a = 2, d = 2\); G.P. \(b = 3, r = 3\)
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Wahi tareeqa jo 6.8.1 mein seekha: pehle \(S_n\) likho, phir poori series ko G.P. ke ratio \(r\) se multiply kar ke \(rS_n\) ek jagah right shift kar ke neeche likho, phir minus karo. Beech mein ek seedhi G.P. ban jati hai jis ka sum hum formula se nikal lete hain. A.G.P. ke sum ka koi ratta formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh tareeqa yaad rakhein.

\(n\)th term
\[T_n = 2n \cdot 3^{n}\]
Kyun: Even numbers ka \(n\)th term \(2n\) hai, aur \(3 \cdot 3^{n-1} = 3^n\). Is liye aakhri yani \(n\)th term \(2n \cdot 3^n\) hai.

\(S_n\) aur \(3S_n\) likhein
\[S_n = 2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^{2} + 6 \cdot 3^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + 2n \cdot 3^{n}\]
\[3S_n = 2 \cdot 3^{2} + 4 \cdot 3^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (2n - 2)3^{n} + 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
Kyun: 3 se multiply karne par har power ek barh gayi. Shift kar ke likha taake \(3^2\) ke neeche \(3^2\), \(3^3\) ke neeche \(3^3\) aaye. \(S_n\) ka second-last term \((2n - 2)3^{n-1}\) tha, jo \((2n - 2)3^n\) ban gaya.

Minus karein
\[-2S_n = 2 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 3^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + 2 \cdot 3^{n} - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
\[-2S_n = 2(3 + 3^{2} + \cdots + 3^{n})\]
\[\quad - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
Kyun: Left side \(S_n - 3S_n = -2S_n\). Right side par har jore ka farq \(2\) times power hai, jaise \((4 - 2)3^2 = 2 \cdot 3^2\). Is sawal mein pehla term \(2 \cdot 3\) bhi isi pattern mein aa jata hai, is liye 2 poori bracket se common nikal aaya.

G.P. ka sum
\[3 + 3^{2} + \cdots + 3^{n}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(3^{n} - 1)}{3 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{3^{n+1} - 3}{2}\]
Kyun: Yahan bracket mein powers 1 se \(n\) tak hain, is liye poore \(n\) terms hain. Pehla term 3, ratio 3.

\(S_n\) nikalein
\[-2S_n = 3^{n+1} - 3\]
\[\quad - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
\[S_n = \dfrac{3 + (2n - 1)3^{n+1}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}[1 + (2n - 1)3^{n}]\]
Kyun: \(2 \times \frac{3^{n+1} - 3}{2}\) mein 2 cancel ho gaya. Phir dono taraf \(-2\) se divide kiya; signs ulat gaye: \(3^{n+1}(2n - 1) + 3\). Aakhir mein \(3^{n+1} = 3 \cdot 3^n\) likh kar \(\frac{3}{2}\) common liya.

Answer key wali shakal se milayein
\[n \cdot 3^{n+1} - (n + 1)3^{n}\]
\[= 3n \cdot 3^{n} - (n + 1)3^{n}\]
\[= (2n - 1)3^{n}\]
Kyun: Answer key jawab \(\frac{3}{2}[1 - (n + 1)3^n + n \cdot 3^{n+1}]\) likhti hai. Upar dikhaya ke us ke andar wala hissa \((2n - 1)3^n\) hi hai, yani dono jawab ek hi hain, sirf shakal mukhtalif hai.

Tasdeeq
\[n = 1:\ \tfrac{3}{2}(1 + 3) = 6 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ \tfrac{3}{2}(1 + 27) = 42 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har sum formula ki sab se aasaan tasdeeq: \(n = 1\) rakho to jawab pehla term aana chahiye, aur \(n = 2\) rakho to pehle do terms ka jama. Agar dono match ho jayein to formula sahi hai. \(S_1 = 2 \cdot 3 = 6\), \(S_2 = 6 + 36 = 42\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(2 + \frac{5}{4} + \frac{8}{4^{2}} + \frac{11}{4^{3}} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh A.G.P. series hai: har term (A.P. ka number) \(\times\) (G.P. ka number) hai. Is ka sum nikalne ke liye koi ratta formula nahi, hum book wala tareeqa lagayenge: \(r\) se multiply karo, ek jagah shift karo, aur minus karo.
Upar wale numbers \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) (\(a = 2, d = 3\)) A.P. hain. Neeche 4 ki powers hain, matlab har term \(\frac{1}{4}\) se multiply ho raha hai: G.P. part \(1, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{4^2}, \ldots\), ratio \(r = \frac{1}{4}\).
Plan: \(T_n\) likho, \(\frac{1}{4}S_n\) shift kar ke neeche likho, minus karo, beech ki G.P. ka sum lagao, aur \(S_n\) nikalo.
Fractions se ghabrana nahi: tareeqa bilkul wahi hai, bas multiply \(r\) ek fraction hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2 + \frac{5}{4} + \frac{8}{4^{2}} + \frac{11}{4^{3}} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) (\(a = 2, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{4}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Wahi tareeqa jo 6.8.1 mein seekha: pehle \(S_n\) likho, phir poori series ko G.P. ke ratio \(r\) se multiply kar ke \(rS_n\) ek jagah right shift kar ke neeche likho, phir minus karo. Beech mein ek seedhi G.P. ban jati hai jis ka sum hum formula se nikal lete hain. A.G.P. ke sum ka koi ratta formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh tareeqa yaad rakhein.

\(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n-1}}\]
Kyun: Upar A.P. ka \(n\)th term aur neeche \(4^{n-1}\), kyunke pehle term ke neeche \(4^0 = 1\) hai, doosre ke neeche \(4^1\). Isi liye power \(n - 1\) hai, \(n\) nahi.

\(S_n\) aur \(\frac{1}{4}S_n\) likhein
\[S_n = 2 + \dfrac{5}{4} + \dfrac{8}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{4}S_n = \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 4}{4^{n-1}} + \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{4}\) se multiply karne par har denominator mein ek 4 aur aa jata hai: \(\frac{x}{4^k}\) ban jata hai \(\frac{x}{4^{k+1}}\). Shift kar ke likha taake same denominator wale terms ek doosre ke neeche hon.

Minus karein
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3}{4^{n-1}} - \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{4^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
Kyun: Left side: \(S_n - \frac{1}{4}S_n = \frac{3}{4}S_n\). Right side par same denominator wale jore ka farq upar sirf \(d\) chhorta hai, kyunke upar A.P. ke numbers hain, misaal ke taur par \(\frac{5 - 2}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\). Pehla term akela rehta hai aur doosri line ka aakhri term minus hota hai.
Dhyan dein: beech wali G.P. ke \(n - 1\) terms hain, \(n\) nahi.

Bracket wali G.P. ka sum
\[\dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{4^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{4}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Kyun: Bracket ki G.P. ka pehla term \(\frac{1}{4}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{4}\) aur terms \(n - 1\) hain. Jab \(r < 1\) ho to \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) wali shakal lagate hain taake denominator positive rahe. \(\frac{1}{4} \div (1 - \frac{1}{4})\) ko pehle alag se hal kar liya.

Simplify kar ke \(S_n\) nikalein
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + 1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 3 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = 4 - \tfrac{4}{3}\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{4}{3}(3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
Kyun: G.P. ka sum rakha: \(3 \times \frac{1}{3} = 1\), is liye bracket seedha khul gaya. \(2 + 1 = 3\). Aakhir mein \(S_n\) ko akela karne ke liye dono taraf \(\frac{4}{3}\) se multiply kiya; \(3 \times \frac{4}{3} = 4\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{4}{3}\) se HAR term ko multiply karna hai, sirf pehle ko nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[n = 1:\ 4 - \tfrac{4}{3} - \tfrac{2}{3} = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ 4 - \tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{5}{12} = \tfrac{13}{4}\]
\[2 + \tfrac{5}{4} = \tfrac{13}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har sum formula ki sab se aasaan tasdeeq: \(n = 1\) rakho to jawab pehla term aana chahiye, aur \(n = 2\) rakho to pehle do terms ka jama. Agar dono match ho jayein to formula sahi hai. Yahan \(S_1 = 2\) aur \(S_2 = 2 + \frac{5}{4} = \frac{13}{4}\); formula dono deta hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(1 + \frac{3}{5} + \frac{5}{5^{2}} + \frac{7}{5^{3}} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh A.G.P. series hai: har term (A.P. ka number) \(\times\) (G.P. ka number) hai. Is ka sum nikalne ke liye koi ratta formula nahi, hum book wala tareeqa lagayenge: \(r\) se multiply karo, ek jagah shift karo, aur minus karo.
Upar wale numbers \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 2\)) A.P. hain. Neeche 5 ki powers hain, matlab har term \(\frac{1}{5}\) se multiply ho raha hai: G.P. part \(1, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{5^2}, \ldots\), ratio \(r = \frac{1}{5}\).
Plan: \(T_n\) likho, \(\frac{1}{5}S_n\) shift kar ke neeche likho, minus karo, beech ki G.P. ka sum lagao, aur \(S_n\) nikalo.
Fractions se ghabrana nahi: tareeqa bilkul wahi hai, bas multiply \(r\) ek fraction hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 + \frac{3}{5} + \frac{5}{5^{2}} + \frac{7}{5^{3}} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 2\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{5}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Wahi tareeqa jo 6.8.1 mein seekha: pehle \(S_n\) likho, phir poori series ko G.P. ke ratio \(r\) se multiply kar ke \(rS_n\) ek jagah right shift kar ke neeche likho, phir minus karo. Beech mein ek seedhi G.P. ban jati hai jis ka sum hum formula se nikal lete hain. A.G.P. ke sum ka koi ratta formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh tareeqa yaad rakhein.

\(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n-1}}\]
Kyun: Upar A.P. ka \(n\)th term aur neeche \(5^{n-1}\), kyunke pehle term ke neeche \(5^0 = 1\) hai, doosre ke neeche \(5^1\). Isi liye power \(n - 1\) hai, \(n\) nahi.

\(S_n\) aur \(\frac{1}{5}S_n\) likhein
\[S_n = 1 + \dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{5}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{5}S_n = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{3}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2n - 3}{5^{n-1}} + \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{5}\) se multiply karne par har denominator mein ek 5 aur aa jata hai: \(\frac{x}{5^k}\) ban jata hai \(\frac{x}{5^{k+1}}\). Shift kar ke likha taake same denominator wale terms ek doosre ke neeche hon.

Minus karein
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2}{5^{n-1}} - \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + 2\left(\dfrac{1}{5} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{5^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
Kyun: Left side: \(S_n - \frac{1}{5}S_n = \frac{4}{5}S_n\). Right side par same denominator wale jore ka farq upar sirf \(d\) chhorta hai, kyunke upar A.P. ke numbers hain, misaal ke taur par \(\frac{3 - 1}{5} = \frac{2}{5}\). Pehla term akela rehta hai aur doosri line ka aakhri term minus hota hai.
Dhyan dein: beech wali G.P. ke \(n - 1\) terms hain, \(n\) nahi.

Bracket wali G.P. ka sum
\[\dfrac{1}{5} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{5^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{5}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{5}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Kyun: Bracket ki G.P. ka pehla term \(\frac{1}{5}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{5}\) aur terms \(n - 1\) hain. Jab \(r < 1\) ho to \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) wali shakal lagate hain taake denominator positive rahe. \(\frac{1}{5} \div (1 - \frac{1}{5})\) ko pehle alag se hal kar liya.

Simplify kar ke \(S_n\) nikalein
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = \tfrac{3}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = \tfrac{15}{8} - \tfrac{5}{8}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{5}{4}(2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
Kyun: G.P. ka sum rakha: \(2 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\), bracket khola, \(1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\). Phir dono taraf \(\frac{5}{4}\) se multiply kiya: \(\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{4} = \frac{15}{8}\), \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5}{8}\).
Dhyan dein: answer key terms ko doosri tarteeb mein likhti hai; tarteeb badalne se jawab nahi badalta.

Tasdeeq
\[n = 1:\ \tfrac{15}{8} - \tfrac{5}{8} - \tfrac{1}{4} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ \tfrac{15}{8} - \tfrac{1}{8} - \tfrac{3}{20} = \tfrac{8}{5}\]
\[1 + \tfrac{3}{5} = \tfrac{8}{5} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har sum formula ki sab se aasaan tasdeeq: \(n = 1\) rakho to jawab pehla term aana chahiye, aur \(n = 2\) rakho to pehle do terms ka jama. Agar dono match ho jayein to formula sahi hai. \(S_1 = 1\) aur \(S_2 = \frac{8}{5}\); dono match.

Diya gaya hai: \(1 + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{7}{9} + \frac{10}{27} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(1, 4, 7, 10, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{3}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Wahi tareeqa jo 6.8.1 mein seekha: pehle \(S_n\) likho, phir poori series ko G.P. ke ratio \(r\) se multiply kar ke \(rS_n\) ek jagah right shift kar ke neeche likho, phir minus karo. Beech mein ek seedhi G.P. ban jati hai jis ka sum hum formula se nikal lete hain. A.G.P. ke sum ka koi ratta formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh tareeqa yaad rakhein.

\(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n-1}}\]
Kyun: Upar A.P. ka \(n\)th term aur neeche \(3^{n-1}\), kyunke pehle term ke neeche \(3^0 = 1\) hai, doosre ke neeche \(3^1\). Isi liye power \(n - 1\) hai, \(n\) nahi.

\(S_n\) aur \(\frac{1}{3}S_n\) likhein
\[S_n = 1 + \dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{7}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{3}S_n = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 5}{3^{n-1}} + \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{3}\) se multiply karne par har denominator mein ek 3 aur aa jata hai: \(\frac{x}{3^k}\) ban jata hai \(\frac{x}{3^{k+1}}\). Shift kar ke likha taake same denominator wale terms ek doosre ke neeche hon.

Minus karein
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + \dfrac{3}{3} + \dfrac{3}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3}{3^{n-1}} - \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{3^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
Kyun: Left side: \(S_n - \frac{1}{3}S_n = \frac{2}{3}S_n\). Right side par same denominator wale jore ka farq upar sirf \(d\) chhorta hai, kyunke upar A.P. ke numbers hain, misaal ke taur par \(\frac{4 - 1}{3} = \frac{3}{3}\). Pehla term akela rehta hai aur doosri line ka aakhri term minus hota hai.
Dhyan dein: beech wali G.P. ke \(n - 1\) terms hain, \(n\) nahi.

Bracket wali G.P. ka sum
\[\dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{3^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Kyun: Bracket ki G.P. ka pehla term \(\frac{1}{3}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{3}\) aur terms \(n - 1\) hain. Jab \(r < 1\) ho to \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) wali shakal lagate hain taake denominator positive rahe. \(\frac{1}{3} \div (1 - \frac{1}{3})\) ko pehle alag se hal kar liya.

Simplify kar ke \(S_n\) nikalein
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + \tfrac{3}{2} - \tfrac{3}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = \tfrac{5}{2} - \tfrac{3}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = \tfrac{15}{4} - \tfrac{9}{4}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{3}{2}(3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
Kyun: G.P. ka sum rakha: \(3 \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\), \(1 + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{2}\). Phir dono taraf \(\frac{3}{2}\) se multiply kiya: \(\frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{15}{4}\), \(\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{4}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{7}{9}\) ko \(\frac{7}{3^2}\) samajhna zaroori hai, warna G.P. part nazar nahi aata.

Tasdeeq
\[n = 1:\ \tfrac{15}{4} - \tfrac{9}{4} - \tfrac{1}{2} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ \tfrac{15}{4} - \tfrac{3}{4} - \tfrac{2}{3} = \tfrac{7}{3}\]
\[1 + \tfrac{4}{3} = \tfrac{7}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har sum formula ki sab se aasaan tasdeeq: \(n = 1\) rakho to jawab pehla term aana chahiye, aur \(n = 2\) rakho to pehle do terms ka jama. Agar dono match ho jayein to formula sahi hai. \(S_1 = 1\) aur \(S_2 = \frac{7}{3}\); dono match.
